title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 157
paragraphs: They lived there for two years; but as they had no prosperity, they left one of their number behind and all the rest sailed to Delphi. Reaching the oracle, they consulted it, saying that though they were living in Libya they were faring no better for it. To them the Pythian priestess made this reply:
“If you, who have not been there, know sheep-rich Libya better than I, who have been there, I marvel at your wisdom.”

Having heard this, Battus and his companions sailed back again; for in fact the god would not release them from the task of settlement until they had come to Libya itself. Arriving at the island and picking up the man they had left behind, they made a settlement in Libya proper, at a spot across from the island called Aziris, enclosed by lovely woods on two sides and with a river flowing along one side.
